slides.say: Given: seven is smaller than two x minus one, in absolute value, which is smaller than nine. Which of the following ranges is possible for x?

A double inequality with bars, and ranges in the choices. We'll solve it three ways, two bands, splitting it in two, and plugging in the answers. [short pause] And there's a bait in the choices, so I'll show you where it comes from.
[short pause] Our first method, two bands. Two x minus one, in bars, is between seven and nine. So the inside is between seven and nine, or, on the negative side, between minus nine and minus seven.
Careful with the negative band. Minus nine is the smaller one, so it goes on the left. Minus nine is smaller than two x minus one, which is smaller than minus seven.

The positive band first. Add one to all three parts. Seven plus one is eight, and nine plus one is ten, so eight, two x, ten. Divide all three by two. Eight over two is four, and ten over two is five. So x is between four and five.

Now a lot of students take one off instead of adding it. Seven minus one is six, nine minus one is eight, and over two that's three to four. That's choice number one, the bait. And choice number four is the same mistake on the negative side.

Four to five isn't in the choices, so on to the negative band. Add one to all three parts. Minus nine plus one is minus eight, and minus seven plus one is minus six. Divide by two. Minus eight over two is minus four, and minus six over two is minus three. So x is between minus four and minus three.
Aaand that's exactly choice number three. On the number line, two small bands, one on each side. Minus four to minus three, and four to five.

[pause] Our second method, splitting it in two. The bars smaller than nine means the inside is trapped between minus nine and nine. Add one, minus eight and ten. Divide by two, minus four and five. So x is between minus four and five.

The bars bigger than seven means the inside is above seven, or below minus seven. Seven plus one is eight, over two is four. Minus seven plus one is minus six, over two is minus three. So x is above four, or below minus three.

Both have to hold. Between minus four and five, and above four, gives four to five. Between minus four and five, and below minus three, gives minus four to minus three. And minus four to minus three is choice number three.
at: Between minus four and five, and below

slides.say: It's longer here, but this split is super useful in other absolute-value questions.

[pause] Our third method, plugging in the answers. If a range is possible, every number in it has to work. So I pick an easy number inside each range, and if it breaks the given, the range is out. Choice number one, three and a half. Two times it is seven, minus one, six. Six isn't bigger than seven, out.
Choice number two, five and a half. Two times it is eleven, minus one, ten. Ten isn't smaller than nine, out.
Choice number three, minus three and a half. Two times it is minus seven, minus one, minus eight. In bars, eight. Between seven and nine, it works.
And choice number four, minus four and a half. Times two is minus nine, minus one, minus ten. In bars, ten. Out.

slides: [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
